channel.title: The Bridge India - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Bridge India (thebridge.in)

item.title: WTT Youth Contender Vadodara: Syndrela Das, Rupam Sardar clinch U-17 singles titles
item.description: Meanwhile, Dev Bhatt and Divija Paul clinched the U13 boys' and girls' singles titles, respectively.

item.title: From Yui Susaki to Aman Sehrawat: Top 5 buys in Pro Wrestling League 2026 Auction
item.description: India's premier franchise-based league is back after a seven-year hiatus, with its 5th season starting on January 15th.

item.title: Soorma Hockey Club part ways with women’s team head coach Jude Menezes
item.description: Rani Rampal appointed interim head coach for remainder of Women’s HIL season following mutual decision.

item.title: Fact Check : Did India win eight medals at the 2024 Olympics as Jay Shah claimed?
item.description: Fact check of ICC Chairman Jay Shah’s statement claiming India won eight medals at the 2024 Paris Olympics.

item.title: WPL 2026 Captains: All five franchises confirm Captains ahead of new season
item.description: Three teams retain their skippers while Delhi Capitals and UP Warriorz opt for leadership changes ahead of WPL 2026.

item.title: Syndrela-Sarthak clinch U-19 mixed doubles titles at WTT Youth Contender Vadodara
item.description: Indian youngsters continue strong showing as Syndrela Das adds another title at the WTT Youth Contender 2026 in Vadodara.

item.title: Senior National Boxing Championships: Amit Panghal, Sagar make winning starts
item.description: Asian Games champion Amit Panghal cruises through his opening bout as heavyweight Sagar survives a tough test on Day 1.

item.title: Kalinga Lancers overturn early setback to defeat Ranchi Royals 4–2 in Men’s HIL
item.description: Brace each from Alexander Hendrickx and Gursahibjit Singh powers Kalinga Lancers to a confident opening win in Chennai.

item.title: Neeraj Chopra to end 10-year-old partnership with JSW Sports
item.description: The two-time Olympic medalist has decided not to renew his contract, which ended in December 2025.

item.title: Neeraj Chopra launches athlete management firm Vel Sports
item.description: Star javelin thrower Neeraj Chopra and JSW Sports announce the conclusion of their formal partnership.
